title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We measure how inserting a deterministic network verifier into a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) loop affects verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we compared: (1) baseline — a single LLM proposal produced once per task, and (2) guarded — the identical shared LLM proposal validated by a deterministic netops verifier and subjected to up to one automated repair iteration if the verifier flagged a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. Primary outcome: verifier pass (no preregistered high/medium-severity violations). Results (complete pairs = 500): baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The archived exact McNemar two-sided test (executor convention: exact binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and model+validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; measured marginal verifier+repair effect on the pass-rate metric is therefore small, though the verifier corrected a single concrete baseline failure (the discordant episode and its validator/repair trace are archived and deterministically locatable in the evidence bundle). All preregistration, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call traces, execution logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being applied to NetOps tasks such as translating operator intent into device configuration, change planning, and automated repair. System and survey literature emphasizes that operational safety depends heavily on surrounding engineering: deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback mechanisms [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A common operational pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and automated or human repairs address violations.

Practitioners need controlled measurements that isolate the marginal contribution of a verifier (holding the model’s proposal fixed). In particular: when an LLM already produces high-quality candidates (on verifier-modeled properties), how much incremental safety does adding a deterministic verifier plus a modest automated repair budget provide on a pass/fail safety metric? We answer this question with a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates verifier+repair impact under canonical deterministic semantics and shared-initial_candidate generation: for each intent→configuration task a single LLM proposal is produced and used both as the baseline submission and as the guarded arm's validated proposal (the guarded arm may apply at most one automated repair iteration if the verifier flags a preregistered high/medium-severity violation).
sections.related_work:
Deterministic and formal verification tools for network configurations (header-space analysis, route-model verifiers, Batfish-style analyzers) provide machine-checkable properties (reachability, isolation, update atomicity) and motivate verifier-in-the-loop designs [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent NetOps/AIOps systems and intent-translation work integrate LLMs for intent parsing and configuration synthesis while advocating engineering guardrails for operational reliability (e.g., INTA, Confucius, other agentic NetOps frameworks) [INTA, 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate→verify→repair patterns appear across structured-generation domains and are proposed to reduce incorrect or unsafe outputs [PoeTone; INTA].

Separate literature documents systemic failure modes of LLM-driven automation (hallucination, overconfidence, tool-integration errors) and recommends verification or human oversight as mitigations [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. What is less prevalent in the supplied record is a controlled, preregistered ablation that quantifies the marginal verifier effect while keeping the LLM’s initial output identical for both arms; our study fills that precise operational gap.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand. We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026, freezing the research question, inclusion/exclusion rules, deterministic task generator seeds, estimands, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule before observing outcomes. Primary confirmatory hypothesis: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the same LLM producing a single proposal without verifier feedback (paired within-task). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline where success == verifier reports zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations. The preregistration and artifacts are archived (preregistration SHA-256 recorded in the execution manifest).

Task corpus, stratification, and inclusion. A deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks was generated using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds and stratified into three clusters per the preregistration: VLAN-change (167), ACL-change (167), and static-route-change (166). All tasks conformed to the verifier’s modeled feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}); no confirmatory exclusions occurred. The full task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and task-level payloads (initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence) are archived in the evidence bundle and confirm realized per-cluster sizes matching the preregistered allocation.

Generation semantics and experimental control. To isolate verifier+repair marginal effect we used generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (independent_condition_generation = false). For each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal recorded once; that identical candidate constituted the baseline output and was also validated by the guarded arm. The guarded path invoked the automated single-repair call only if the deterministic verifier reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation on the shared candidate. This design prevents conflation with verifier-guided regeneration and isolates the effect of verification plus at most one repair applied to the same initial proposal.

Models, adapter, and verifier. Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (provider recorded as openai_responses); model parameters (execution/model_configuration.json) include max_output_tokens = 2000 and single-attempt generation. The deterministic verifier used for gating and scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator specification and the violation-code→severity mapping are archived in validator-spec artifacts). The guarded arm permitted at most one automated repair iteration per preregistration.

Statistical analysis and exact implementation. The preregistered confirmatory test is the exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes. The archived analysis executor implements the exact two-sided McNemar by forming the discordant-pair count n = n10 + n01 and performing an exact binomial test on the observed n10 (executor discordant-ordering convention: n10 = guarded-only successes). Two-sided p is computed from the Binomial(n, 0.5) distribution per the archived executor; paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs were computed with B = 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) drawing 500 paired units with replacement. Missingness and retries: preregistered retry policy allowed up to two automated retries for transient model-provider errors; execution accounting and logs record exact retry and provider-call events.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes. The execution completed with completed_episode_count = 1000 (shared_initial_generation = 500; repair-stage calls observed = 1) and model_calls_used = 501. Aggregated per-condition counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 499, baseline failures = 1 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998); guarded successes = 500, guarded failures = 0 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table (guarded × baseline) is n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002. The paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729).

Exact McNemar two-sided p-value. Using the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs implementation yields p = 1.00 for the observed discordant counts (n = 1, n10 = 1); the archived analysis_log.jsonl documents the executor parameters and the p-value calculation.

Discordant episode provenance and deterministic retrieval. Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1; that single repair produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1): the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass. The run archives per-task validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, and the repair prompt/response for the discordant episode in execution/raw_results.jsonl and associated provider-call traces. To deterministically locate and inspect that episode within the archived artifacts: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for entries where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and guarded scoring indicates a pass (guarded pass == 1). The execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm exactly one such episode exists; the run-level artifact summary records model_calls_used = 501 and repair-stage calls = 1. We do not reproduce the raw per-episode identifier inline here; the archived raw_results.jsonl contains the immutable per-episode identifiers and full validator/repair traces for deterministic audit.

Power and ceiling effect. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline error prevalence ≈ 0.30; observed baseline failure prevalence (1/500) produced a ceiling effect that reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute improvements. Consequently, secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative due to near-zero counts. Analysis artifacts (missingness_summary.csv, paired_contingency_table.csv, deterministic_reconciliation.json) document these counts and confirm no exclusions or failures occurred during execution.
sections.discussion:
Conditional operational interpretation. Under the constrained experimental regime—requested LLM gpt-5-mini, shared_initial_candidate semantics, a deterministic verifier modeling a limited feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and at most one automated repair iteration—the LLM produced near-ceiling correct proposals on the verifier-modeled properties and the measured marginal pass-rate benefit of adding the verifier was small (0.002). This demonstrates a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal quality is extremely high with respect to verifier-scoped properties, modest verifier+repair budgets may produce negligible composite pass-rate gains even while correcting rare concrete failures (the single archived discordant episode).

Design-choice implications and operational trade-offs. The shared-initial_candidate semantics intentionally answer the operational question of marginal verifier benefit when deployments preserve an original proposal for human review or when model-call budgets are tightly constrained. Alternative semantics—verifier-guided regeneration, multiple repair iterations, or search-in-the-space-of-candidates—may yield larger final-pass probabilities at the cost of additional model calls and higher latency. Execution accounting (model_calls_used = 501; repair-stage calls = 1) provides an artifact-backed cost baseline to inform such trade-offs.

Threats to validity. Internal validity is strengthened by preregistration, deterministic seeds, and automated replacement rules; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity is limited by the verifier’s modeled property set and severity mapping: pass == no high/medium-severity violations is defined relative to validator coverage (validator-spec artifacts archived). External validity is limited by single-model testing, a synthetic deterministic task corpus, and restricted feature scope; results do not generalize to other LLMs, broader device CLIs, or dynamic protocol state properties outside the verifier scope. Conclusion validity is constrained by the low observed baseline error rate (ceiling effect) and the resulting small number of discordant pairs.
sections.conclusion: We ran a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated verifier+single-repair impact under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The LLM produced near-ceiling verifier-scoped proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the run’s exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention). This conditional measurement shows that when baseline proposal quality is very high for verifier-modeled properties and the verifier’s coverage is limited, marginal pass-rate benefits from a modest verifier+repair budget can be negligible on a composite pass/fail metric, though the verifier can still correct rare concrete failures (one archived discordant episode). Practitioners should (1) measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative data before allocating repair budgets, (2) align verifier coverage with operator-critical constraints, and (3) choose generation/repair semantics to match deployment priorities. All preregistration, code, prompts, model outputs, validator traces, provider-call logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the evidence bundle for deterministic re-inspection of every claim made here.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model family (gpt-5-mini requested) and a single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality is made.
Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets or iterative regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) created a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the archived exact-binomial-on-discordant-pairs convention and the small discordant count.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
